chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not go to the chicks in their nests, nor to the birds in their sleep.' A man asked: 'And what is its sleep, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'The night is its sleep, so do not visit it during its sleep. And do not go to the chicks in its nest until it has grown feathers and flown. When it flies, then draw your bow for it and set your snare for it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on hunting young birds or disturbing them at night?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *adab al-sayd* (hunting etiquette) by distinguishing between the night as the resting period for birds and the day for activity, ensuring the young have fully matured before being hunted. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on mercy and avoiding waste (*israf*) in resource extraction, linking the physical act of hunting to spiritual discipline. The instruction to 'set your bow' and 'place your snare' only after flight indicates a transition from passive waiting to active engagement, mirroring the balance between patience and effort in religious practice.
